before.title: Galilean limiting chart maps and bounded chart regions
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains")
before.design_state: definition of the family of affine chart maps whose bounded-region limit is proved in lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts
before.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and $c>0$ with the SI conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]], let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame with inertial chart $x$ and spatial Euclidean structure $(S,\delta,|\cdot|)$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and write the points of $\mathbb R\times S$ as $(t,x)$.

(a) *Lorentz boost charts with a variable speed scale.* For $v\in S$ and a real $C>|v|$ put $\gamma_C(v):=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ ([[def-rational-power]]) and define the affine map $\Phi_{v,C}:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $$\Phi_{v,C}(t,x):=\Bigl(\gamma_C(v)\bigl(t-\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2}\bigr),\ \ x+\tfrac{\gamma_C(v)-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)\,v-\gamma_C(v)\,t\,v\Bigr)\quad(v\ne0),$$ with $\Phi_{0,C}:=\mathrm{id}$; at $C=c$ this is the coordinate expression, in the convention $x^0=ct$, of the passive Lorentz boost $B(v/c)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]]: if an event has coordinates $(ct,x)$ in the unprimed inertial chart of the frame, then $\Phi_{v,c}(t,x)$ are its coordinates $(x'^0/c,\,x'^1,x'^2,x'^3)$ in the boosted inertial chart with parameter $v/c$.

(b) *Galilean boost.* For $v\in S$ define the affine map $G_v:\mathbb R\times S\to\mathbb R\times S$ by $G_v(t,x):=(t,\,x-tv)$.

(c) *Bounded chart region.* For reals $T,R>0$ put $D_{T,R}:=\{(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S:|t|\le T,\ |x|\le R\}$, with $|\cdot|$ the norm of the named frame.

(d) *Scope of the family.* The parameter $C$ is a variable speed scale inside a family of coordinate expressions; it is not a change of the model's adopted constant $c$, and the members with $C\ne c$ are auxiliary mathematical maps used only to state the limit of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]. Nothing here asserts a physical limit of the framework, and no limiting trajectory, force or interaction is defined.
before.strategy: A definition item. Well-definedness: for $v\ne0$, $C>|v|$ the number $\gamma_C(v)$ is a rational power of the positive base $1-|v|^2/C^2$ ([[def-rational-power]]), and the displayed formulas assign to each pair $(t,x)$ a pair of elements of $\mathbb R\times S$ using the bilinear form $\delta$ and scalar multiplication in $S$; for $v=0$ the middle term is $0/0$ and the map is declared separately to be the identity (the same convention as [[def-lorentz-boost]]). The identification at $C=c$ is a substitution, not a claim: writing $\beta:=v/c$ and $x^0:=ct$ in the definition of $B(\beta)$ of [[def-lorentz-boost]] gives $x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta\cdot x)$ and $x'=x+((\gamma-1)/|\beta|^2)(\beta\cdot x)\beta-\gamma\beta x^0$, that is $x'^0/c=\gamma_C(v)(t-\delta(v,x)/C^2)$ and the displayed spatial formula, because $\beta\cdot x=\delta(v,x)/C$, $|\beta|^2=|v|^2/C^2$ and $\beta x^0=(v/C)(ct)=vt$. No Lorentz property, no limit and no physical interpretation is asserted; those are the contents of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]].

references.title: B. Crowell, Special Relativity, revision 2020-12-10 (author-published undergraduate textbook, 246 PDF pages); signature (+---) converted to (-+++) and c = 1 formulas restored to x^0 = c t; Section 4.2 pp. 82-86 (relativistic kinetic energy; Example 5 p. 86, the Newtonian prediction eV = (1/2)mv^2), Section 4.3.3 Example 8 p. 91 (the Newtonian limit v = p/m), Section 4.3.4 pp. 95-96 (p = m gamma v; the momentum of a material particle approaches infinity as its speed approaches c) and problems 11-12 p. 117 (expand K = m(gamma-1) and p = m gamma v in Taylor series; show the first terms are the nonrelativistic expressions)

S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997); signature (-+++) with c = 1. Chapter 1 Section 1.5 printed p. 27 (PDF p. 34): for small v, p^0 = m + (1/2)mv^2 (rest energy plus kinetic energy) and p^1 = mv (Newtonian momentum); Chapter 4 Section 4.1 printed pp. 105-106 (PDF pp. 112-113): the Newtonian limit, the slow-motion condition (4.10) and the weak static field

before.title: Uniform Galilean limit of the boost charts on bounded regions, and its failure on unbounded regions
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains"); prose-scaffold.md SR11 row (Carroll slow-motion discussion pp. 105-106)
before.design_state: complete explicit bound-and-limit argument on the bounded chart region from the pair's own definitions and the uniform Taylor remainder
before.statement:
Let $v\in S$, $T,R>0$, and let $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, $G_v$ and $D_{T,R}$ be as in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]. For $C>|v|$ write $\gamma_C:=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ write $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=(t',x')$.

(a) *Exact differences.* For every $C>|v|$ and all $(t,x)$,
$$t'-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\frac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2},\qquad x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv),$$ where $x_\parallel:=\delta(v,x)v/|v|^2$ for $v\ne0$; for $v=0$ one has $\Phi_{0,C}=\mathrm{id}$ and both differences vanish.

(b) *Uniform bounds on bounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$, every $C>|v|$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$,
$$|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\frac{|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T).$$

(c) *Uniform convergence to the Galilean chart map.* For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon>|v|$ such that for every $C\ge C_\varepsilon$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$, $$\max\{|t'-t|,\,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\le\varepsilon .$$ Hence $\sup_{D_{T,R}}\max\{|t'-t|,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\to0$ as $C\to\infty$ with $v,T,R$ fixed, the convergence is uniform on $D_{T,R}$, and for each fixed $(t,x)$ the image $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)$ converges to the Galilean value $G_v(t,x)=(t,x-tv)$.

(d) *Failure on unbounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$ and every $C>|v|$, $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|t'-t|=+\infty$ and $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|x'-(x-tv)|=+\infty$; so the boundedness of $T,R$ in (c) is essential and the limit is not uniform on the whole chart domain.
before.strategy:
(a) Substitute the definition: $t'-t=\gamma_Ct-\gamma_C\delta(v,x)/C^2-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\delta(v,x)/C^2$; and $x'-(x-tv)=\tfrac{\gamma_C-1}{|v|^2}\delta(v,x)v-\gamma_Ctv+tv=(\gamma_C-1)\bigl(\tfrac{\delta(v,x)}{|v|^2}v-tv\bigr)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv)$, using $\gamma_C-1=(\gamma_C-1)$. The case $v=0$ is the separate definition.

(b) Take absolute values in (a) and use the triangle inequality ([[lem-of-triangle-inequality]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]): $|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)|t|+\gamma_C|\delta(v,x)|/C^2$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)|x_\parallel-tv|$. Writing $v=\sum v^ie_i$, $x=\sum x^ie_i$ in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis of [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]] gives $\delta(v,x)=\sum_i v^ix^i$, so [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]] yields $|\delta(v,x)|\le|v|\,|x|$, and $|x_\parallel|=|\delta(v,x)|/|v|\le|x|$, hence $|x_\parallel-tv|\le|x|+t|v|$ by the triangle inequality; with $|t|\le T$, $|x|\le R$ this gives the two displays.

(c) Put $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, so $\gamma_C=f(z)$ with $f$ of [[lem-sr-uniform-low-speed-taylor-remainder]] ([[def-rational-power]]); that lemma gives $|\gamma_C-1|\le z\bigl(\tfrac12+K(z_0)z_0\bigr)$ for every $z_0\in(0,1)$ with $z\le z_0$ and the quantitative convergence $f(z)\to1$ as $z\to0^+$. Fix $\varepsilon>0$, choose $z_1\in(0,1)$ so small that $|\gamma_C-1|\le\tfrac12$ whenever $z\le z_1$ (so $\gamma_C\le\tfrac32$) and $|\gamma_C-1|\bigl(T+R+|v|T\bigr)\le\tfrac\varepsilon2$; such $z_1$ exists by the display of the Taylor lemma. Now if $C\ge\max\{|v|,|v|/z_1\}$ then $z=|v|^2/C^2\le|v|/C\le z_1$ (because $|v|/C\le1$), and with $C^2\ge 2\cdot\tfrac32|v|R/\varepsilon=\tfrac{3|v|R}{\varepsilon}$ we also get $\gamma_C|v|R/C^2\le\tfrac32|v|R/C^2\le\tfrac\varepsilon2$. Hence both bounds of (b) are at most $\varepsilon$ for every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$: this is $C_\varepsilon:=\max\{|v|,|v|/z_1,\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}$ (with the harmless convention $z_1$ chosen first). Uniformity in $(t,x)$ is exactly the supremum over $D_{T,R}$, and pointwise convergence follows from containment of each point in a bounded region.

(d) For the family $(t,x_\lambda):=(0,\lambda v/|v|)$ with $\lambda>0$ we have, by (a), $x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)\lambda v/|v|$, whose $\delta$-norm is $(\gamma_C-1)\lambda\to\infty$ as $\lambda\to\infty$ (since $\gamma_C>1$ for $v\ne0$); and for $(t,x)=(0,-\mu v)$ with $\mu>0$ we get $t'-t=\gamma_C\delta(v,\mu v)/C^2=\gamma_C\mu|v|^2/C^2\to\infty$ as $\mu\to\infty$. So both suprema are infinite.

after.title: Uniform Galilean limit of the boost charts on bounded regions, and its failure on unbounded regions
after.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains"); prose-scaffold.md SR11 row (Carroll slow-motion discussion pp. 105-106)
after.design_state: complete explicit bound-and-limit argument on the bounded chart region from the pair's own definitions and the uniform Taylor remainder
after.statement:
Let $v\in S$, $T,R>0$, and let $(\Phi_{v,C})_{C>|v|}$, $G_v$ and $D_{T,R}$ be as in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]. For $C>|v|$ write $\gamma_C:=(1-|v|^2/C^2)^{-1/2}$ and $z:=|v|^2/C^2$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathbb R\times S$ write $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)=(t',x')$.

(a) *Exact differences.* For every $C>|v|$ and all $(t,x)$,
$$t'-t=(\gamma_C-1)t-\gamma_C\frac{\delta(v,x)}{C^2},\qquad x'-(x-tv)=(\gamma_C-1)(x_\parallel-tv),$$ where $x_\parallel:=\delta(v,x)v/|v|^2$ for $v\ne0$; for $v=0$ one has $\Phi_{0,C}=\mathrm{id}$ and both differences vanish.

(b) *Uniform bounds on bounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$, every $C>|v|$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$,
$$|t'-t|\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\frac{|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T).$$

(c) *Quantitative rate and uniform convergence to the Galilean chart map.* Fix $z_0\in(0,1)$ and set $K_0=\tfrac38(1-z_0)^{-5/2}$, $A_0=\tfrac12+K_0z_0$ and $\Gamma_0=(1-z_0)^{-1/2}$. Whenever $v\ne0$ and $C\ge |v|/\sqrt{z_0}$, the following hold uniformly on $D_{T,R}$: $$|t'-t|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2T+\Gamma_0|v|R}{C^2},\qquad |x'-(x-tv)|\le\frac{A_0|v|^2(R+|v|T)}{C^2}.$$ Thus the rate is $O(C^{-2})$ with explicit constants for fixed $v,T,R,z_0$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon>|v|$ such that for every $C\ge C_\varepsilon$ and every $(t,x)\in D_{T,R}$, $$\max\{|t'-t|,\,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\le\varepsilon .$$ For $v\ne0$, put $H=T+R+|v|T$, choose any $z_1$ with $0<z_1\le\min\{z_0,(2A_0)^{-1},\varepsilon/(2A_0H)\}$ (for example the displayed minimum), and set $$C_\varepsilon=\max\{|v|/\sqrt{z_1},\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}.$$ This is sufficient, and since $z_1<1$ it gives $C_\varepsilon>|v|$. For $v=0$ both errors vanish identically and any $C_\varepsilon>0$ suffices. Hence $\sup_{D_{T,R}}\max\{|t'-t|,|x'-(x-tv)|\}\to0$ as $C\to\infty$ with $v,T,R$ fixed, the convergence is uniform on $D_{T,R}$, and for each fixed $(t,x)$ the image $\Phi_{v,C}(t,x)$ converges to the Galilean value $G_v(t,x)=(t,x-tv)$.

(d) *Failure on unbounded regions.* For every $v\ne0$ and every $C>|v|$, $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|t'-t|=+\infty$ and $\sup_{\mathbb R\times S}|x'-(x-tv)|=+\infty$; so the boundedness of $T,R$ in (c) is essential and the limit is not uniform on the whole chart domain.
after.strategy:
(a) Subtract the Galilean values from the definition: t'-t=(gamma_C-1)t-gamma_C delta(v,x)/C^2 and x'-(x-tv)=(gamma_C-1)(x_parallel-tv). For v=0 both maps are the identity and both differences vanish.

(b) Scalar absolute-value triangle inequality gives |t'-t|<=(gamma_C-1)|t|+gamma_C|delta(v,x)|/C^2. In a delta-orthonormal basis, thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite gives |delta(v,x)|<=|v||x|. The spatial inner-product norm's homogeneity and triangle inequality are cor-triangle-inequality-for-inner-product-norm: |x_parallel|=|delta(v,x)|/|v|<=|x|, hence |x_parallel-tv|<=|x_parallel|+|-tv|<=|x|+|t||v|. The absolute value of t is essential for negative chart times. Since gamma_C>=1, |t|<=T and |x|<=R, substitution proves both bounded-region displays.

(c) Fix z0 in (0,1). For 0<=z=|v|^2/C^2<=z0, the Taylor supplier's first remainder bound gives 0<=gamma_C-1<=z/2+K0 z^2<=A0 z. Positive-base rational-power monotonicity and reciprocal order give gamma_C<=(1-z0)^(-1/2)=Gamma0. Substitute into (b) to obtain both explicit C^-2 bounds. For epsilon>0, set H=T+R+|v|T>0 and choose 0<z1<=min{z0,1/(2A0),epsilon/(2A0H)}; each entry of the minimum is positive. For C>=|v|/sqrt(z1), z<=z1, so gamma_C-1<=A0 z1<=1/2 and (gamma_C-1)H<=epsilon/2. Thus gamma_C<=3/2. If also C>=sqrt(3|v|R/epsilon), the additional time term gamma_C|v|R/C^2<=epsilon/2, so both error bounds from (b) are <=epsilon on the whole bounded region. Because z1<=z0<1 and |v|>0, the first threshold is strictly larger than |v|; the inadmissible boost boundary C=|v| is excluded. For v=0 handle the identity family separately with any positive threshold. Supremum over the bounded region gives uniform convergence; each fixed point lies in such a region, giving pointwise convergence.

(d) For v nonzero and fixed C>|v|, gamma_C>1. At (t,x)=(0,lambda v/|v|), lambda>0, the spatial error norm is (gamma_C-1)lambda, unbounded as lambda increases. At (t,x)=(0,-mu v), mu>0, the time error is gamma_C mu |v|^2/C^2, unbounded as mu increases. Thus both whole-domain suprema are infinite. This is a coordinate-family limit only; it changes no physical postulate, adopted constant c, trajectory, force or interaction. No omitted expression or qualitative smallness choice replaces a quantitative step.

before.title: Worked uniform Galilean chart bound on a bounded region
before.reference: scaffold/special-relativity.md SR11 reservation ("explicit Galilean limiting chart maps with bounded domains")
before.design_state: explicit numerical instance of the exact differences, the uniform bounds and the epsilon choice
before.statement:
Take $v=e_1$ (so $|v|=1$), $T=1$, $R=2$ and the point $(t,x)=(1,2e_1)$ in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]], and let $\Phi_{v,C}(1,2e_1)=(t',x')$. Then for $C=10$: $\gamma_C=(99/100)^{-1/2}=10/\sqrt{99}=10/(3\sqrt{11})\approx1.0050378153$, $t'\approx0.9849370590$, $x'\approx1.0050378153$, so with the Galilean value $G_v(1,2e_1)=(1,e_1)$,
$$|t'-t|\approx0.0150629410\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\tfrac{|v|R}{C^2}\approx0.0251385716,$$ $$|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0050378153\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T)\approx0.0151134458 ;$$ for $C=100$ the same quantities are $\gamma_C\approx1.0000500038$, $|t'-t|\approx0.0001500063\le0.0002500138$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0000500038\le0.0001500113$. The observed deviations shrink by the factors $\approx100.4$ and $\approx100.7$ when $C$ grows from $10$ to $100$, consistent with the $O(1/C^2)$ rate of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]\,(b). Finally, for the tolerance $\varepsilon=0.01$ the same lemma's proof requires only $z\le z_1$ with $z_1\approx1/900$ and $C^2\ge3|v|R/\varepsilon=600$; the choice $C=30$ satisfies both and gives $|t'-t|\approx0.0016674389$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0005560189$, both below $0.01$. All decimals are rounded values of the exact expressions; the example asserts no physical interpretation of the family $\Phi_{v,C}$.
before.strategy: Substitute the data into the definition: $\delta(v,x)=\delta(e_1,2e_1)=2$ and $|v|=1$, so $\gamma_C=(1-1/C^2)^{-1/2}$, $t'=\gamma_C(1-2/C^2)$ and $x'=2+2(\gamma_C-1)-\gamma_C$ by [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]]; the displayed values are the evaluations at $C=10$ and $C=100$, with $\gamma_{10}=10/(3\sqrt{11})$ and $\gamma_{100}=(9999/10000)^{-1/2}$ computed through [[lem-rational-power-laws]] and [[thm-of-square-roots]], rounded to ten significant digits. The two bound comparisons are the inequalities of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]\,(b) at $(t,x)=(1,2e_1)\in D_{1,2}$; the ratio check is the quotient of the rounded deviations. The $\varepsilon=0.01$ instance is the explicit choice of the lemma's proof with $z_1=1/900$, $|\gamma_C-1|(T+R+|v|T)\le\ldots$ evaluated at $C=30$; every comparison is arithmetic in $\mathbb R$ and no claim about the model's constant $c$ is made, because $C$ is the auxiliary speed scale of the definition.

after.statement:
Take $v=e_1$ (so $|v|=1$), $T=1$, $R=2$ and the point $(t,x)=(1,2e_1)$ in [[def-sr-galilean-limiting-charts]], and let $\Phi_{v,C}(1,2e_1)=(t',x')$. Then for $C=10$: $\gamma_C=(99/100)^{-1/2}=10/\sqrt{99}=10/(3\sqrt{11})\approx1.0050378153$, $t'\approx0.9849370590$, $x'\approx1.0050378153$, so with the Galilean value $G_v(1,2e_1)=(1,e_1)$,
$$|t'-t|\approx0.0150629410\le(\gamma_C-1)T+\gamma_C\tfrac{|v|R}{C^2}\approx0.0251385716,$$ $$|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0050378153\le(\gamma_C-1)(R+|v|T)\approx0.0151134458 ;$$ for $C=100$ the same quantities are $\gamma_C\approx1.0000500038$, $|t'-t|\approx0.0001500063\le0.0002500138$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|\approx0.0000500038\le0.0001500113$. The observed deviations shrink by the factors $\approx100.4$ and $\approx100.7$ when $C$ grows from $10$ to $100$, consistent with the explicit $O(1/C^2)$ rate of [[lem-sr-uniform-galilean-limit-of-boost-charts]]\,(c). The ratios of the exact deviations, evaluated before rounding, are approximately 100.4154227043 and 100.7487483984, respectively. Finally, for tolerance $\varepsilon=0.01$, take $z_0=1/4$. Then $K_0=4\sqrt3/9$ and $A_0=1/2+\sqrt3/9<3/4$. Choose exactly $z_1=1/900$. With $H=T+R+|v|T=4$, one has $z_1<z_0$, $A_0z_1<1/1200<1/2$ and $A_0Hz_1<1/300<\varepsilon/2=1/200$, so every threshold inequality is satisfied. The sufficient threshold is $$C_\varepsilon=\max\{1/\sqrt{z_1},\sqrt{3|v|R/\varepsilon}\}=\max\{30,\sqrt{600}\}=30>1=|v|.$$ Thus $C=30$ is sufficient uniformly on $D_{1,2}$. At the specified point $\gamma_{30}=30/\sqrt{899}$, $|t'-t|=1-449/(15\sqrt{899})\approx0.0016674389$ and $|x'-(x-tv)|=30/\sqrt{899}-1\approx0.0005560189$, both below $0.01$. The whole-region bound values at $C=30$ are approximately $0.0027794768$ and $0.0016680568$, also below $0.01$. All displayed decimals are rounded to ten places after the decimal point and all inequalities compare exact values. No physical interpretation of the auxiliary $\Phi_{v,C}$ family is asserted.
after.strategy: With delta(e1,2e1)=2 and |v|=1, put g_C=C/sqrt(C^2-1). The definition gives gamma_C=g_C, t'=(C^2-2)/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and x'=g_C e1; the Galilean value is (1,e1). At C=10,30,100, t'<1: both sides are positive, and (C^2-2)^2<C^2(C^2-1) is equivalent to 4<3C^2. Thus the exact deviations are d_t(C)=1-(C^2-2)/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and d_x(C)=C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1. The exact uniform bound values from lemma(b) are B_t(C)=C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1+2/(C sqrt(C^2-1)) and B_x(C)=3(C/sqrt(C^2-1)-1). Evaluate these exact radical expressions at the three scales, then round to ten places after the decimal point. Ratios are evaluated from the exact radical expressions, not already rounded deviations: d_t(10)/d_t(100)=100.4154227043 to ten decimal places and d_x(10)/d_x(100)=100.7487483984 to ten decimal places, hence 100.4 and 100.7 to one decimal place. For the tolerance proof, z0=1/4 gives K0=(3/8)(3/4)^(-5/2)=4sqrt(3)/9 and A0=1/2+sqrt(3)/9<3/4, since sqrt(3)<9/4 follows by squaring the positive quantities: 3<81/16. Therefore z1=1/900 is positive, <=z0, A0 z1<1/1200<1/2 and A0 H z1<1/300<1/200=epsilon/2. This proves z1<=min{z0,1/(2A0),epsilon/(2A0H)} explicitly. The sufficient threshold is |v|/sqrt(z1)=30, while sqrt(3|v|R/epsilon)=sqrt(600)<30 because 600<900; hence C_epsilon=30>|v|. The lemma therefore controls both errors uniformly on the entire bounded region. Exact radical evaluation gives the stated point and bound values at C=30. No ellipsis or empirical claim is used, and the fixed model scale c is not varied.
